assumptions: The initial product remains retrospective QA analytics and technician training support for one imaging modality; it does not diagnose, determine clinical acceptability, or instruct a retake.
All images are treated as potentially identifiable personal data, and any pilot proceeds only under documented clinic and reseller rights with an appropriate GDPR role and safeguards.
A reseller can technically export images and reliable repeat or defect labels from a bounded installed base, although interoperability and access have not been demonstrated.
The quoted pilot budget excludes any extensive medical-device conformity program; final qualification, class, notified-body need, and full cost remain unresolved.
Pricing, reseller share, gross margin, renewal, site count, and the founder-equity path are scenario assumptions rather than validated commercial results.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: A vendor-neutral retrospective layer sold through resellers could turn recognized repeat analysis into device-specific training and service intelligence across heterogeneous clinic fleets. The core image-quality function is not novel, however, because named imaging vendors already advertise adjacent or directly overlapping QA capabilities.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Quality assurance and repeat analysis are recognized audit activities under radiological-practice guidance and EU requirements. A mature department's 0.93% repeat rate shows that avoidable-retake savings can be too small to fund the offer, while separate willingness to pay for training, audit evidence, or service reporting remains unknown rather than disproven.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Per-location recurring revenue and a reseller bundle could generate predictable cash flow, but 55-70% hypothesized gross margin must absorb channel share, secure image handling, device-specific integration, support, expert review, and regulated maintenance. The path needs roughly 3,000 multi-country sites, and conformity costs outside the pilot estimate could exceed the founder's bootstrap capital.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: One reseller, one modality, and 5-10 clinics is a disciplined starting segment, and Poland's sizeable practising-dentist base indicates a nontrivial underlying market. The number of compatible imaging locations with actionable repeat problems, independent budget, and reseller reach is not established, so the economically qualified beachhead may be much smaller.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Vendor neutrality and reseller alignment could create a niche across mixed installed bases. Overjet and Duerr Dental already advertise close substitutes, full imaging systems can bundle QA at little visible incremental price, and no privileged reseller relationship or unique cross-vendor dataset currently supports segment domination.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Validated retrospective analytics could expand to additional modalities, reseller territories, technician training, service diagnostics, and eventually live assistance. New devices and countries add interface and compliance work, while live acquisition guidance would require a materially harder regulatory and clinical-validation path.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Consented images linked to device, technician, repeat, error-cause, and outcome labels could create a valuable cross-vendor benchmark asset. Data rights, reliable labels, and scale are all unresolved, and imaging vendors or larger AI incumbents are better positioned to access workflow data and bundle competing features.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: A neutral layer could serve reseller fleets that no single imaging vendor covers and provide consolidated training reports. There is no demonstrated accuracy, interoperability, workflow improvement, compliance benefit, or economic advantage over bundled vendor QA, so the behavior-changing value proposition is presently only plausible.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Modern image models and digital radiography make automated retrospective analysis increasingly practical, and QA duties provide a durable reason to review performance. The regulatory obligations are longstanding and direct incumbents are already active, so there is no clear temporary window or underserved regulatory shock.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Resellers can bundle the module into installation or annual service, concentrate access to clinics, and reduce the founder's need for continuous direct selling. No reseller commitment exists, vendor-bundled alternatives reduce reseller motivation, and the same intermediary controls access, support burden, commercial terms, and renewal.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: Image modelling suits the founder's neuroscience and data-science background, and a retrospective single-modality pilot is bounded. GDPR roles, re-identification risk, uncertain MDR qualification, expert oversight, unreliable labels, and non-guaranteed DICOM or proprietary interoperability create a heavy execution stack near the founder's full available capital.

main_structural_strength: A reseller-bundled, vendor-neutral QA layer can reach a heterogeneous installed base through an existing service relationship while using repeat and defect outcomes to build cross-vendor benchmarks.
primary_score_limiter: The standalone value pool may be too small in experienced clinics, while direct incumbent overlap and the combined cost of image access, integration, privacy, and possible medical-device compliance constrain margins and reseller appetite.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: A mature dental radiology department reported only a 0.93% repeat rate, and two established vendors already market image-quality or acquisition-QA functions, directly challenging both the savings case and differentiation.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A formal intended-purpose classification opinion, a signed reseller and lawful data arrangement, and a 5-10-clinic single-modality pilot showing reliable exports and labels, a material actionable QA gap, improvement beyond bundled tools, low integration/support cost, and payer renewal intent at the proposed price.
highest_value_structural_change: Make the reseller the payer for an annual service-contract QA audit on one modality, begin with locally processed repeat metadata and expert-reviewed benchmark reports, and defer image-level modelling until data rights, classification, and incremental value are proven; this reduces privacy, regulatory, integration, and low-retake-economics exposure at the initial wedge.
